notes: EBIT is modeled as Operating income from the Consolidated Statements of Income (GAAP). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/100885/000010088526000037/unp-20251231.htm))
D&A is modeled as Depreciation from the income statement (no separate amortization line was used). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/100885/000010088526000037/unp-20251231.htm))
Capex is modeled as absolute 'Capital investments' cash flow line (cash used in investing activity). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/100885/000010088526000037/unp-20251231.htm))

NWC construction (net operating working capital) uses: (current assets minus cash and short-term investments) - (current liabilities minus debt due within one year). Negative NWC values reflect a working-capital deficit. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/100885/000010088526000037/unp-20251231.htm))
Forecast drivers are base-case assumptions, not company guidance; only modest growth/margin changes are applied in bull/bear scenarios.

WACC is set using a railroad industry proxy (Weighted Average Cost of Capital) from the Washington State Department of Revenue study; this is not a company-specific WACC from UP filings. ([dor.wa.gov](https://dor.wa.gov/sites/default/files/2025-04/2025COCRailroads.pdf))

Comps EV/NTM Revenue and EV/NTM EBITDA are treated as forward/NTM proxies using EV/Sales and EV/EBITDA from the same WSDOR study; NTM is not guaranteed by source methodology. ([dor.wa.gov](https://dor.wa.gov/sites/default/files/2025-04/2025COCRailroads.pdf))
NOL balance/utilization were not identified as a standalone disclosed NOL carryforward amount in the 2025 10-K content retrieved here; set to null.

catalysts: STB process milestones for a revised UP–NS submission (completeness and subsequent review schedule). ([stb.gov](https://www.stb.gov/news-communications/latest-news/pr-26-02/))

Sustained operating ratio improvement and service/productivity metrics supporting EBIT margin stability in 2026+. ([up.com](https://www.up.com/press-releases/financial/4q25-earnings-announcement-260127))

Capital plan execution and incremental safety/efficiency initiatives affecting cash conversion and reinvestment efficiency. ([up.com](https://www.up.com/press-releases/financial/4q25-earnings-announcement-260127))
company_overview: Union Pacific is a Class I freight railroad serving the U.S. western two-thirds, with one reportable rail operating segment. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/100885/000010088526000037/unp-20251231.htm))
The 2025 10-K reports total operating revenues of $24.51B and operating income (EBIT) of $9.85B. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/100885/000010088526000037/unp-20251231.htm))

The company highlights ongoing operational improvements (safety, service, productivity) alongside a multi-year capital program. ([up.com](https://www.up.com/press-releases/financial/4q25-earnings-announcement-260127))
current_context: UP reported full-year 2025 operating revenue of $24.5B (+1% YoY) and operating ratio of 59.8% (adjusted 59.3%). ([up.com](https://www.up.com/press-releases/financial/4q25-earnings-announcement-260127))

2026 outlook emphasizes muted economic forecast, pricing dollars in excess of inflation dollars, mid-single digit EPS growth, and a $3.3B capital plan. ([up.com](https://www.up.com/press-releases/financial/4q25-earnings-announcement-260127))

Merger process update: STB found the UP–NS major merger application incomplete (without prejudice), directing resubmission steps. ([stb.gov](https://www.stb.gov/news-communications/latest-news/pr-26-02/))
investment_highlights: Base-case volume/price dynamics translated into modest forward revenue growth (low-to-mid single digit range). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/100885/000010088526000037/unp-20251231.htm))

EBIT margin is modeled as stable-to-slightly expanding, consistent with continued operating ratio improvement into 2027+ (precision scheduled railroad operating model). ([up.com](https://www.up.com/press-releases/financial/4q25-earnings-announcement-260127))

Capital intensity is kept consistent with recent replacement/enhancement capex levels (capital investments ~15% of sales). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/100885/000010088526000037/unp-20251231.htm))

Working capital is modeled as a persistent deficit (negative NWC), reflecting the company’s balance-sheet structure (accounts payable and other current liabilities exceed cash-adjusted current assets). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/100885/000010088526000037/unp-20251231.htm))
key_risks: Macro/volume risk: freight demand softness could reduce revenue and operating leverage versus the modest base-case growth path. ([up.com](https://www.up.com/press-releases/financial/4q25-earnings-announcement-260127))
Regulatory/transaction risk: merger timing/conditions (and costs) can alter investor expectations and capital allocation. ([stb.gov](https://www.stb.gov/news-communications/latest-news/pr-26-02/))
Cost inflation and labor/operational risk could pressure the EBIT margin trajectory from precision-scheduled operating improvements.

valuation_summary: DCF base case uses a Gordon-growth terminal approach with a modest long-run growth rate and an industry WACC proxy from a Washington State railroad cost of capital study. ([dor.wa.gov](https://dor.wa.gov/sites/default/files/2025-04/2025COCRailroads.pdf))

Comps are anchored to forward EV/EBITDA and EV/Sales multiples for Class I railroads from the same cost of capital study, with forward P/E added where available. ([dor.wa.gov](https://dor.wa.gov/sites/default/files/2025-04/2025COCRailroads.pdf))
Scenario work keeps operating efficiency changes modest (growth and margins) while stress-testing terminal assumptions via WACC/terminal growth.
